title: A per-thread request context

blocks.text: Thread-local variables work on virtual threads: each virtual thread has its own copy of a `ThreadLocal` value. With a million virtual threads, though, every value left behind is memory held for nothing, so the page's rule is to `remove()` the value in a `finally` block when the work is done.
Write `RequestContext`, which holds "the user of the current request" per thread:

items: `runAs(String user, Callable<T> work)` makes `user` the current user of the **calling thread**, runs `work` there and returns its result. When it returns, **or throws**, the calling thread has no current user again. An exception from `work` is passed on unchanged.
`current()` returns the current user of the calling thread, or `null` outside `runAs`.
Threads never see each other's user, and a thread started from inside `runAs` does not inherit it.

rows: `runAs("ann", ...)` on one virtual thread while `runAs("bob", ...)` runs on another
each work sees its own user

cases.says: Inside runAs, current() is the given user, and runAs returns the work's result.
Two virtual threads inside runAs at the same time each see their own user.
After runAs returns, current() is null again on that thread.
When the work throws, runAs passes the exception on and current() is null again.
A thread started from inside runAs sees no user: the user belongs to the calling thread only, and is not inherited.

concepts: Each virtual thread has its own ThreadLocal value, and the value is removed in finally when the work ends.
